system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**CONFIDENTIAL – BUYER LEGAL ADVICE: PROJECT KESTREL**  
**Counterparty:** Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller)  
**Target:** Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd  
**Our Principal:** Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Amelia Frost, decision authority)  

---

## 1. MATERIAL DEPARTURES FROM PLAYBOOK & REQUIRED PUSHBACKS

| # | Issue | Seller Position | Playbook Requirement | Gap / Risk | Required Pushback |
|---|-------|----------------|---------------------|------------|-------------------|
| **1** | **General Warranty Cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8M (Cl 12.1) | **25% / AUD 6M baseline**. 20% only with **Amelia Frost written authority** (none given). | Seller imposes our fallback as opening bid without authority. | **Reject 20%. Counter at 25% / AUD 6M.** No fallback without Frost sign-off. |
| **2** | **Thresholds (De Minimis / Basket)** | De minimis AUD 25K; Basket AUD 250K, **excess-only** recovery (Cl 12.2) | De minimis **AUD 5K**; Basket **AUD 50K**, **first-dollar** liability once exceeded. | 5× de minimis, 5× basket, and “excess-only” shifts all sub-basket risk to Buyer. | **Insist on AUD 5K / AUD 50K first-dollar basket.** Excess-only is non-starter. |
| **3** | **General Claims Period** | 18 months (Cl 12.3/13) | **24 months baseline**. 18 months only with **Frost written approval** (none). | Seller treats fallback as baseline; also adds “all Claims unless expressly stated” catch-all. | **Hold 24 months.** Delete “applies to all Claims” language—it swallows fundamental/fraud regimes. |
| **4** | **Fundamental / Title Warranties** | Same caps, baskets, time limits as general warranties “for administrative simplicity” | **Separate regime**: 100% cap, ≥6 years, **outside** general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. | Seller collapses title/capacity into general regime—eliminates buyer’s core protections. | **Require standalone fundamental regime** (100% cap, 6+ yr, no basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier). |
| **5** | **Fraud / Wilful Concealment / Deliberate Misconduct** | Limitations, exclusive remedy & non-reliance apply to **“all Claims of any nature”** (Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | **Full carve-out** from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, non-reliance—**non-waivable**. | Seller’s “all Claims” clause expressly guts fraud carve-out. | **Insert express fraud/wilful misconduct carve-out** overriding Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5. Mark non-waivable. |
| **6** | **Disclosure Standard** | General disclosure of **entire data room (DD-002–DD-012) + public registers + statutory registers** (Sch 7, Disc Ltr [1.1]–[1.2]) | **Specific fair disclosure only**. Reject whole-data-room, public-register, prudent-search deemed disclosure. | Seller dumps 11 DD items + public records as “disclosed”—buyer cannot track what was fairly disclosed. | **Strike general disclosure clauses.** Require schedule of specifically identified, page-referenced disclosures. |
| **7** | **Buyer Knowledge Exclusion** | “No claim for any matter Buyer or advisers had knowledge, **including discoverable from data room/public records**” (Cl 8.3) | **Delete blanket exclusion**. Any qualifier: named Seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry. **Never excuses title, capacity, fraud, specific indemnity.** | “Discoverable” standard + adviser knowledge + data-room sweep = near-total warranty evisceration. | **Delete Cl 8.3.** If Seller insists on knowledge qualifier: named individuals, reasonable enquiry, **explicit carve-outs for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities**. |
| **8** | **Bluefen Consent (Material Customer)** | **Reasonable endeavours**; consent “satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent” (Cl 3/6.3) | **Effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion**. Reasonable endeavours insufficient. Consent-on-delivery unacceptable. | No final consent; conditions (Cl 11.3) unverified; “reasonable endeavours” gives Seller exit. | **Condition Precedent: written Bluefen consent + certified satisfaction of Cl 11.3 conditions**. No “reasonable endeavours” fallback. |
| **9** | **Riverlark Debt (AUD ~3.2M)** | Release “to be provided **following Completion**” (Cl 2/7) | **Current payout from Completion funds + effective security releases**. Post-completion release only with **irrevocable undertaking + Frost approval**. | No repayment at Completion; security remains; Seller controls timing. | **Funds-flow mandate: Riverlark paid out at Completion, discharges delivered at Completion.** If Seller insists on post-Completion: irrevocable undertaking + Frost sign-off. |
| **10** | **Employee Completion Bonuses (DD-005: AUD 420K + on-costs)** | “Matter for Seller; **not separately itemised in funds flow**” | **Specific line item or Seller-funded**; on-costs (payroll tax, super) included; funds flow must not silently exclude. | Bonuses + on-costs (~AUD 500K+) disappear from completion mechanics—Buyer effectively pays twice. | **Insert dedicated funds-flow line for bonuses + on-costs**, paid from Seller proceeds or escrowed. Seller to confirm grossed-up amount. |
| **11** | **Ironquay IP Indemnity (SOW3, AUD 180K)** | Existing indemnity **limited to SOW3 payment only**; “considered adequate” (Cl 11.1) | **Broaden indemnity** (preserve SOW3 cure); AUD 180K **not independently verified** either way. | Narrow indemnity leaves Buyer exposed to IP ownership/licence gaps beyond SOW3 fees. | **Expand indemnity to cover IP title, third-party claims, breach of IP warranties**; retain SOW3 payment cure. Require bank verification of AUD 180K status. |
| **12** | **Export/Privacy Incident (DD-006)** | “Preliminary operational matter; **not expected to be material**” (Cl 4.6/Sch 6) | **Preserve logs, investigate, require updates**; assume **NO confirmed breach/harm/notification duty/numeric demand** either way. | Seller pre-judges materiality; no contractual obligation to continue investigation or notify Buyer of developments. | **Specific covenant**: preserve evidence, continue investigation, provide fortnightly updates until Completion + 6 months post. Indemnity for any resulting liability (outside general caps). |
| **13** | **Tax / IP Warranties** | “Settled under the general regime above” | **OPEN**—assume **no unlimited liability, no resolution**. Separate regimes, not folded into 20% cap. | Seller tries to cap tax/IP exposure at AUD
=== END ADVICE ===
